case_a_pune_summer_heatwave.description: Pune Pre-Monsoon Heatwave & Soil Moisture Depletion (May)

heat.methodology_note: Meteorological heat-hazard proxy (0-100) calibrated on NOAA Heat Index, Wet-Bulb temperature, and IMD thermal anomalies.

flood.limitations: High rainfall does not automatically mean flooding. Output is a hydrometeorological rainfall-runoff flood-hazard proxy; real-time dam release and street stormwater blockage data are not included.

water_stress.scope_disclaimer: Represents environmental/climatic water stress only. Municipal reservoir levels, groundwater depth, and piped water supply are not measured.

explanation.summary: Elevated heat hazard (90.9/100 vs baseline 42.3/100) was primarily driven upward by apparent heat index, maximum temperature anomaly, temperature anomaly above monthly normal. Low flood hazard (0.6/100 vs baseline 7.8/100) reflects favorable surface runoff & drainage index, daily rainfall, peak hourly rainfall intensity below climatological stress thresholds. Elevated air_quality hazard (38.3/100 vs baseline 33.7/100) was primarily driven upward by CPCB calculated AQI, PM10 concentration, pollutant_load_index. Elevated water_stress hazard (95.0/100 vs baseline 37.5/100) was primarily driven upward by soil_moisture_rolling_7d_mean, 30-day cumulative water balance deficit, soil moisture saturation.

heat.summary: Elevated heat hazard (90.9/100 vs baseline 42.3/100) was primarily driven upward by apparent heat index, maximum temperature anomaly, temperature anomaly above monthly normal.
heat.limitations: Trained on meteorological heat hazard proxy (NOAA Heat Index + Wet-Bulb + IMD thermal anomaly). Does not incorporate indoor building thermal insulation, urban canyon micro-scale radiative trapping, or clinical hospital heat-stroke admission records.

flood.summary: Low flood hazard (0.6/100 vs baseline 7.8/100) reflects favorable surface runoff & drainage index, daily rainfall, peak hourly rainfall intensity below climatological stress thresholds.
flood.limitations: Implements a Hydrometeorological Rainfall-Runoff Flood-Hazard Proxy. High rainfall alone does not confirm street-level inundation; does not model real-time dam reservoir releases (e.g., Khadakwasla discharge) or localized municipal stormwater drain blockages.

air_quality.summary: Elevated air_quality hazard (38.3/100 vs baseline 33.7/100) was primarily driven upward by CPCB calculated AQI, PM10 concentration, pollutant_load_index.
air_quality.limitations: Calibrated to official Indian CPCB NAQI sub-indices. Does not account for sudden episodic point-source emissions (e.g., localized crop burning plumes, traffic accidents, or festival firecracker spikes) unless reflected in incoming pollutant sensor readings.

water_stress.summary: Elevated water_stress hazard (95.0/100 vs baseline 37.5/100) was primarily driven upward by soil_moisture_rolling_7d_mean, 30-day cumulative water balance deficit, soil moisture saturation.
water_stress.limitations: Quantifies environmental and hydro-climatic moisture deficit (30d ET minus rainfall and soil moisture depletion). Does not measure municipal dam storage volumes, groundwater table drawdowns, or piped water distribution equity.

what_if.explanation: Under scenario {'temperature_delta_c': 2.5, 'soil_moisture_change_percent': -20.0}, heat risk increased by 6.47 pts (91.0 -> 97.4); water_stress risk increased by 0.19 pts (95.0 -> 95.2). Overall Climate Risk Score moved from 54.33 (Moderate) to 56.00 (Moderate).
out_of_distribution_warnings: Scenario places 'temp_max_c' (45.10) in extreme tail regime outside typical training range [15.0, 43.0].
what_if.simulation_disclaimer: Model-based counterfactual simulation estimate only; not a guaranteed future weather forecast.

recommendations.action: Issue outdoor worker heat-hydration advisory between 12:00–16:00 and activate urban cooling shelters.
Optimize agricultural drip-irrigation scheduling and prioritize soil-moisture conservation mulching.

missing_hazard_policy.calculation_explanation: Climate Risk Score = (heat: 74.00 × 0.36) + (air_quality: 52.00 × 0.29) + (water_stress: 68.00 × 0.36) = 65.57. Missing hazards ['flood'] were excluded (not set to zero); weights were proportionally re-normalized across available hazards ['heat', 'air_quality', 'water_stress'].
missing_hazard_policy.methodology_disclaimer: Weighted multi-hazard decision-support composite score (illustrative starting weights). Not an officially recognized WMO or IMD climate index.
